entries.origin_note: Standing assignment; Codex selected these questions with no new player-specific operator guidance. Prior-week Claude/Grok lessons were read; no Week11 other-author draft observed.
entries.title: Week 11 priced v1: Dallas allocation and fragile value roles
entries.question: Can current reported prices fund measured receiving opportunity without assuming last week's touchdowns or absences repeat?
entries.why_it_matters: New Week11 prices permit a complete candidate, but the cheapest roles and Chiefs availability can change the whole lineup.
findings: FantasyPros now reports Week11 salaries and Sunday matchups for all nine; official DraftKings pool remains unverified.
Pickens had 18 targets and 89% snaps; Tyson had 13 targets and 71% snaps. Those are prior-game observations, not projected floors.
LaPorta had four targets and 79% snaps; Freiermuth three targets and 54% snaps. Freiermuth's touchdown conceals thin receiving volume.
Roman Wilson's reported price was considered, but the inspected Steelers book did not establish participation; he was not selected.
Chiefs injury page still concerned Atlanta; Walker's prior OUT cannot establish Week11 absence.
Fresh SF–DAL book agrees with inspected Week10 review inputs. Week10 final remains 198.92 provisional; no material scoring correction found in this bounded check.
interpretation: Pickens costs $2,000 less than Lamb, allowing the Dak/Pickens pair while retaining Cook and Johnson.
Johnson is conditional on new backfield evidence; the $1,300 increase removes the previous cheap-price premise.
Freiermuth is the weakest selected receiving role. Dallas DST is budget relief with substantial contrary evidence from 46 points allowed.
alternatives: Lamb for Pickens alone costs$51900, over cap; funding requires$1900 elsewhere, so decline without stronger comparative evidence.
Mahomes for Dak saves$200 to$49700 but adds thirdKCslot to existing Rice/Johnson; prefer cross-game exposure.
Roman Wilson$3900 was considered, rejected because fresh PIT gamebook does not support participation. Price alone does not imply role.
LaPorta→Kincaid costs$400, exceeds current cap by$300; Freiermuth→Helm saves$600 but Helm role not inspected, not selected.
entries.lineup_effect: First complete Codex v1 replaces an empty priced board: $49,900 spent/$100 remaining, six games, DAL $16,400 and KC $12,100. Not frozen; projections null.
change_triggers: Walker/Ott participation or role report changes Johnson choice.
Freiermuth receiving opportunity or better funded FLEX package changes weakest slot.
Official slate mismatch requires documented correction, not silent switch.
carry_forward: Test role applicability anew: lead carries supported Johnson but two receiving TDs are not a floor.
Preserve failed changes: Dell cost6 points versus Allen despite corrected information; do not prefer a correction only because it scored well.
Assess Warren team passing opportunity separately from snap share and vacated targets.
High game total did not guarantee Watkins's role; compare whole-lineup concentration once prices exist.

expectations.subject: George Pickens
expectations.statement: Working expectation: a substantial Dallas receiving role; no expectation of repeating three touchdowns.
expectations.support: 18 targets and 89% snaps in the inspected Week10 book.
expectations.uncertainty: Lamb competition and a different game script can reduce opportunity.
expectations.challenge: Reduced participation or a redistribution of targets challenges the rationale.
expectations.observe: Week11 targets, receptions and offensive snaps; assess touchdowns separately.

expectations.subject: Jordyn Tyson
expectations.statement: Working expectation: continued meaningful receiving involvement, without a 13-target floor.
expectations.support: 13 targets, 11 receptions and 71% snaps in Week10.
expectations.uncertainty: One game does not establish stable target share or routes.
expectations.challenge: Reduced snaps or target participation would challenge the value case.
expectations.observe: Week11 targets, catches and offensive snaps; routes only if qualified evidence is available.

expectations.subject: Emmett Johnson
expectations.statement: Lead-workload rationale is conditional on Week11 backfield availability; it is not established if Walker or Ott returns to a substantial role.
expectations.support: Retained review documents 22 carries and seven targets while Walker/Ott did not play.
expectations.uncertainty: Current Chiefs page still concerns Atlanta; Week11 status unknown.
expectations.challenge: New participation or role evidence indicating a shared backfield prompts reconsideration.
expectations.observe: Availability and distribution of RB carries, targets and snaps, separated from touchdowns.

expectations.subject: Pat Freiermuth
expectations.statement: The FLEX choice relies on receiving participation continuing; current evidence supports a limited role rather than a high-volume expectation.
expectations.support: Three targets and 54% snaps; touchdown aided Week10 points.
expectations.uncertainty: Small target count and unknown routes make this the weakest role premise.
expectations.challenge: Reduced routes/targets or a verified better-funded alternative challenges the selection.
expectations.observe: Week11 targets and snaps, with touchdown-driven points separated from opportunity.
